Theme

Money, work & business

fund noun

money set aside for a purpose

also set aside money, emergency fund, reserve fund, pension fund, common fund, kitty

classical

Liv. 1.53.3: captīvam pecūniam in aedificātiōnem ejus templī sēposuit
Cic. Att. 15.15.3: id ego ad illud fānum sēpositum putābam
Levi–Bini p. 28: pecūnia for fondo, money meant for a purpose

pecūnia sēposita

noun and participle

money set aside (for a purpose)

Latin names the money and what it is put aside for: pecūniam in rem sēpōnere.

Other words

  • aerārium, aerāriī n. — a treasury; a fund held in common

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Nep. Arist. 3.1: id enim commūne aerārium esse voluērunt; Suet. Aug. 49.2: aerārium mīlitāre; Liv. 27.10.11: in sānctiōre aerāriō, the reserve kept for the worst emergencies

    Classically the state treasury in the temple of Saturn, and so any fund held in common: the Delian League’s, or the fund Augustus set up to pay soldiers on their discharge (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • captīvam pecūniam in aedificātiōnem ejus templī sēposuit

    he set the captured money aside for building the templeLiv. 1.53.3

  • Id enim commūne aerārium esse voluērunt.

    For they wanted this to be their common fund.Nep. Arist. 3.1

  • aerārium mīlitāre cum vectīgālibus novīs cōnstituit

    he set up a fund for the soldiers, with new taxes to keep it filledSuet. Aug. 49.2

See also money, resources, investment, bank.

SourcesLewis & Short: pecunia · Lewis & Short: sepono · Lewis & Short: aerarium
